newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile supermarket firm Jumbo invests in Argentina.
newsitem.headline: Chile supermarket firm Jumbo invests in Argentina.

text.p: Chilean supermarket chain Jumbo will invest $100 million in building three hypermarkets in Buenos Aires, said general manager Stefan Krausse.
"Besides these new stores, we will have other outlets in the provinces where Jumbo has bought land, like in the city of Mendoza," Krausse told reporters.
Jumbo already operates five hypermarkets in Buenos Aires and has three in Chile, the latest of which was opened officially Thursday.
The firm, which does not trade on the stock market, is the second Chilean firm to announce major investments in Argentina this week.
The D&S supermarket chain said Monday it will invest $400 million in the next three years on expanding its network of stores in Chile and Argentina.
Chileans are Latin America's most frequent supermarket shoppers with 90 percent of domestic shopping in Santiago done in supermarkets, officials have said.
